decisions.reason: Although launched as a flagship, the lack of later website presence and its crop-specific use make it more likely the firm will discontinue it as a standard product and redirect resources elsewhere.
A foldable large container line is close to the firm's core reusable-packaging business, so it is more likely to be retained even if its web presentation was later consolidated or changed.
Stackable plastic crates fit the firm's mainstream offer and are likely to stay, though weak later visibility raises some risk of consolidation into a broader crate range.
A medium-duty rackable pallet line serves core logistics applications for industrial customers, making continued retention more likely than withdrawal.
The spill-retention pallet line is more specialized than the firm's main transport-packaging range and its absence from later website evidence suggests a higher chance of being pruned.
This pallet variant appears relatively niche and may be better handled through custom or broader pallet offerings than as a separate marketed product.
